entities.summary: Iraqi Maqam is a genre of Arabic maqam music found in Iraq. The roots of modern Iraqi maqam can be traced as far back as the Abbasid Caliphate, when that large empire was controlled from Baghdad. The ensemble of instruments used in this genre, called Al Chalghi al Baghdadi, includes a qari' (singer), santur, goblet drum, joza, cello, and sometimes oud and naqqarat. The focus is on the poem sung in classical Arabic or an Iraqi dialect. A complete maqam concert is known as fasl and is named after the first maqam: Bayat, Hijaz, Rast, Nawa, or Husayni. Iraqi maqam is a music genre. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Iraqi maqam genre has had a significant regional impact on Arabic music and culture, with its unique ensemble of instruments and focus on classical Arabic poetry. Its influence can be seen in the development of other Middle Eastern musical styles.
